quest.title: Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble
quest.description: After navigating an incredibly cumbersome procedure, you take on an assignment related to the Fontaine Research Institute. But before you can officially begin, though, you have to undergo a final review...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Primogem x60, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6, Unknown Item #363354 x1

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: ...This adventurer didn't pass the review either. I wonder what's wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did someone not pass the Guild review?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME}. *sigh* I'm afraid that this isn't really a Guild affair, but a commission from the Fontaine Research Institute.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: I'm sure you've heard that the full name of the Fontaine Research Institute is "Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering." Before the... explosion, it was the technological center of the entire Court of Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think I've heard of it before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon remembers! Someone named Edwin made a mistake, and there was an explosion at the Fontaine Research Institute, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A commission from a place that blew up once? Sounds dangerous.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: That is true. According to the Fontaine Research Institute, the commission is rather difficult, and not for just anyone.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: So those who want to give it a try must go to the specified location to undergo a series of qualification reviews, and they must prepare their own documents and certifications.

choices.text: Is a Mondstadt flying license acceptable?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: As an addendum, yes. They actually have a list of documents that you must bring.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: The list includes your current and previous Adventure Handbooks, your commissions from the last eighty days, and more. Some of them even require stamps from the Maison Gestion.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: And that's not all. Even if adventurers have all the documents and proofs ready, and arrive at the specified location to be reviewed...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: They will not be able to accept the commission if they fail just one item of the qualification review.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: If the adventurer is not willing to accept other work arrangements, then they will be rejected.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That sounds really strict.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Yes, a lot of them went excitedly, only to return angry. This commission has become so infamous that no one wants to be reviewed anymore.

choices.text: Now I'm kind of interested...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: You want to be reviewed!? That... That would be a huge help!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't get too excited...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Thank you for lending the Guild your aid! Please wait here while I get all the required documents ready for you.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Do you have a pen? Oh, don't worry, I'll go get a few bottles of ink.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A... few bottles? Is one not enough?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: I... can't say. But don't worry, I'm very familiar with these documents, so just follow my instructions.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: First, one proof of your adventure qualifications, one thirty-day travel history, and one registration of past and current Adventure Handbook serial numbers...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Now for your commission history, income statement, commission evaluations, commission statistics, and average positive ratings.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: For your resume, fill in your habitual residence, contact address, contact information, emergency contact, your current name, names you've used in the past, any pseudonyms, and aliases that you use when you want to conceal your identity.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Now you have to sign the good faith commitment, a notice of liability, a notice of obligation, and a notice of exemptions on information release for legal purposes. And...

choices.text: This monologue's great, give us another!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, that's a lot of documents.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: With Katheryne's help, you start filling out the forms. Alternating between hesitance and doubt, you use up bottle after bottle of ink, but the stack of forms also gradually shrinks. As you finish the last form, both Katheryne and you breathe a sigh of relief...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Finally! So this commission's complete, then?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It hasn't even started!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon didn't think this commission would be so troublesome. But if we don't go to the review, then we've wasted our time...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Well then, we'll leave this commission to you!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I haven't even passed the qualification review yet.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: You'll be fine, I believe. As the receptionist of the Adventurers' Guild, I know what you're capable of.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: If Fontaine Research Institute rejects you, then there's no one else in Fontaine who can take this commission.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: I'll mark the location on the map. Go there and find someone named Desnos, who is stationed there and will guide you.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Thank you again. You've done the Guild a huge favor!

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: *sigh* If possible, I'd prefer to not have to stamp a single adventure qualification more. The way this is going, I'm going to wear the stamp out...

choices.text: My writing hand is tired from just listening to the list of documents.
That sounds challenging.
Is an arrest warrant a document?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: I think it counts as identification, but may not be something you want to submit. Anyway, they have a list of documents that you must bring.

dialogues.speaker: Thick Files
dialogues.text: (All those signed documents from before. Now they lie here quietly, and will not object to anything.)

talks.objective: Go to the preliminary review location

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why does Katheryne look so stressed out?

dialogues.speaker: Lanty
dialogues.text: I—It's exploded again!? The financial reports... I don't think there's any way to recover them now...
There's no end to these stupid meka! Oh, my lovely, muscular legs are now full of these horrid welts and bruises...
Thank you, friend. If it weren't for you, I'd still be taking a beating from those meka...

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: Oh, sorry, I forgot to introduce myself. I'm Desnos, a member of the Fontaine Research Institute, an assistant researcher... Or so I used to be.

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: Now I'm responsible for receiving the adventurers who come here for recruitment and conducting preliminary qualification reviews.

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: They're called preliminary qualification reviews, but it's more just me checking if they're carrying all the proper documents with them.

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: After all, some adventurers can't even get their documents right...

choices.text: Adventurers who come here for recruitment?

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: Yes, as you said, we've been asking the Adventurers' Guild to recruit adventurers who can investigate and search the ruins of the Fontaine Research Institute.

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: After all, nearly the entire Institute was destroyed in the explosion, and we don't have a lot of manpower.

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: This violates the Institute's non-disclosure agreements and some other work regulations, of course, but technically only on paper...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think I've heard of this incident before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon remembers! Someone named Edwin made a mistake, and there was an explosion at the Institute, right?

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: Oh, so everyone knows, do they? Ugh, must've been some journalists from The Steambird with nothing better to do...

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: Anyway, that's what happened, and that's where we're at now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In other words, you're looking for people who are good at searching for things in ruins?

choices.text: We're good at that.

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: I can see that you're more confident than ordinary people, and I believe you've got good reason for that kind of confidence. I'm glad you're interested in the commission.

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: But if you really are planning to take it up, I'll have to ask you to fill out some simple forms.

choices.text: Like the other adventurers?

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: Yes, your comprehension and attention are excellent... Better than ones who came before you, anyway.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like a lot of work. We don't usually have to jump through all these hoops when we take a commission...

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: Well, the commission concerns confidential items within the Fontaine Research Institute. The ruins contain scholarly papers and research results that must be retrieved.

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: These are assets of the Fontaine Research Institute, and they are the foundation for rebuilding the Institute — indeed, the hope of the entire Court of Fontaine!

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: Only trustworthy, upright, elite adventurers may enter the ruins, and that's why we have to run a qualification review. It's also why I'm here to do the preliminary part of it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... and how many elite adventurers have you recruited so far?

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: Um, well, it's complicated. The ones I had high hopes for declined because they were in bad shape at the time. Anyway, at this point, well... Alright, we have none.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are your standards too high? How else would you end up not finding a single adventurer.

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: These are the rules set by Mr. Choiseul, and I can't do anything about it. In fact, I have even helped many adventurers to polish up their documents.

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: But even so, no adventurers have passed the review set by Mr. Choiseul and Mr. Raimondo.

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: But don't worry, you're already much better than the previous ones, so your chances of passing are certainly higher.

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: Please sit here while I go get a few bottles of ink. We'll be filling out some forms.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A... few bottles? Is one not enough?

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: Based on my experience, if you didn't bring any documents, then one bottle is definitely not enough.

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: First, one proof of adventure qualifications, one thirty-day record of travel history...

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: Actually, I'm sure that the Adventurers' Guild has these records. Don't worry, I'll write you an official letter to explain the situation, and we'll request said documents from the Guild.

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: But for the resume, you'll have to fill in your habitual residence, your contact address, contact information, your current name, names you've used in the past, your pseudonyms, and aliases that you use when you want to conceal your identity.

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: Then, you have to sign the good faith commitment, a notice of liability, a notice of obligation, and...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: With Desnos's help, you start filling out the forms. Alternating between hesitance and doubt, you use up bottle after bottle of ink, but the stack of forms also gradually shrinks. As you finish the last form, Desnos smiles and you breathe a sigh of relief...

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: That's all the documents. Now you just need to go to the Institute itself for the final review.

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: I was meant to be the one to take you there, but those stupid meka injured my leg.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's okay! Just tell us where it is, and we'll head on over there ourselves!

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: Sounds good. I'll mark the location down on your map... Oh, and by the way! I suggest you head straight to the roof and talk to Mr. Nacker.

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: The Institute sent him to work in the area. You can go talk with him. There are lots of clockwork meka in the nearby wilds, so he's definitely going to need a formidable guard.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait. We haven't passed your final review yet. Why are you assigning us work already?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And there's no compensation either.

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: Well now, just hear me out — Mr. Nacker's a senior researcher at the Fontaine Research Institute who once even did research under Edwin, so he's got some sway in the institute.

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: If you were to get along well with him and "incidentally" demonstrate your capabilities to him to prove your worth... then you're gonna have much better chances at passing the review!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what you're saying is that we should help this Mr. Nacker, and thank him for the privilege while we're at it?

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: Precisely. You can tell him: "Before arriving at the Fontaine Research Institute for the final review, Mr. Desnos has first tasked me with being your guard and ensuring your safety."

response.speaker: Desnos
response.text: Anyway, I won't hold you up any longer. He should be on the roof. I've still got to... Ouch, my leg... Those stupid meka...

choices.text: Is this the qualification review?
This doesn't sound too hard.
So, you're looking for adventurers?

Thank you, friend. If it weren't for you, I'd still be taking a beating from those meka...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, tell me about the Institute's commission...

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: Ah! You're here for the recruitment too? Sorry, please excuse my manners. Let's talk business then, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: Did you bring all the documents with you? If not, I can help you with the ones you're missing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Got 'em all right here.

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: Good. Let's see...

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: One proof of adventure qualifications, and one thirty-day travel history, all nice and clear. This'll do just fine.

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: Uh... I notice you've only got one Adventure Handbook with you. I'm gonna need you to show me all the Adventure Handbooks you've used and are currently using so I can take a photo of them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is the only one I have...

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: Well, you're quite the young and promising one then... Ahem! No matter. It's easier having everything in one book anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: Now for your commission history, income statement, commission evaluation info, commission statistics, and average positive ratings... Hmm, you're very hardworking, and you've quite the income, too!

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: Good faith commitment, a notice of liability, a notice of obligation, and a notice of exemptions on information release for legal purposes. The last one wasn't really that necessary, but... oh well. Still...

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: Very good! Well done. All your documents are with you. Thank heavens! You're the only candidate within the past two weeks who actually prepared all the proper documents.

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: Now all you need to do is go to the Fontaine Research Institute to undergo a final review.

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: I was meant to be the one to take you there, but those stupid meka injured my leg.

I've said this many times, Ms. Chronie. Rebuilding the Fontaine Research Institute is our only goal right now.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: You've said the same thing three times now. Hmph. I know all too well that when you guys start repeating things like robots, there's definitely something big that you're trying to hide.
...Think what you like. As for the numerous issues you mentioned earlier, I suggest you go talk to Mr. Raimondo.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: What, is he going to tell me all the things the Fontaine Research Institute is hiding?
No, but his ways of beating around the bush might be more sincere.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: You...
Anyway, Ms. Chronie... I have my own business to attend to. The one next in line has been waiting for quite a while now.
Hello, how can I help you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you Mr. Nacker?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Yes, I am.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You introduce yourself to Nacker and describe the final review situation. Upon mentioning Desnos, you remember what he last told you...\n"Before formally arriving at the Fontaine Research Institute for the final review, Mr. Desnos has first tasked me with being your guard and ensuring your safety."

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: #I see. Thank you for applying, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}... and I suppose I must also thank Mr. Desnos's injured leg.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Hmm... The wilds around here do pose many dangers, and having an adventurer capable of passing the preliminary qualification review by my side would be a lot safer.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: I can't act like I didn't hear that. What dangers are there exactly, if I may ask? According to the investigations, lots of Arkhium flew out of the Institute when it exploded.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Will the uncontrolled Arkhium radiate energy? Will it contaminate the surrounding environment?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Wouldn't this entire area be contaminated, then?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I suddenly feel somewhat short of breath...

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: That's just your imagination at work. *sigh* After leaving its catalytic environment, Arkhium immediately returns to an inert state. It won't radiate or contaminate anything.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: It is apparent that Ms. Chronie's way of phrasing her concerns brought you unnecessary misunderstandings.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Miss} {NICKNAME}, may I take another look at your documents? If you really wish to escort me, then we'll have to take something of a detour.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: I'm going to a few nearby places to review the technological assets of the Institute and nab some documents along the way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who's this lady next to you...

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Some reporter, that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: #Indeed, that is what I am. It's a great honor to meet you, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}. I've heard your name from my colleagues many times before.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: I'm Chronie, a journalist for the political affairs section of The Steambird. If you have time, could we arrange a time to have a chat?

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: And of course, Ms. Paimon is also welcome to join. I'm very interested in your adventures.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Let me see... How does next Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday sound to you guys? Even this Saturday could work. We could go for a cup of coffee.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Or how about right now? You guys stay here and chat, and I'll go about my work duties.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: #That won't do. I've already reserved today's entire interview schedule for you. Sorry, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Paimon, we'll have to chat another time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's okay! We've got work to do today anyway!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We need to escort Mr. Nacker first...

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: *sigh* I must stress again that I'm just an ordinary researcher now, and I have no further information to give you.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Plus, we've also got tedious and meaningless work ahead of us. Even if you go ahead and interview me, you won't get any useful information from it.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: That won't be a problem, Mr. Nacker. All work has its own unique value, and it's our job to uncover it... Don't worry about me.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: #...Suit yourself then. Let's get going, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: According to the schedule, there's a document we need to get at the institute's Executive Office. Hopefully, Conjat wasn't called up for some other work...

talks.objective: Go to the Executive Office of Fontaine Research Institute

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: Darn it... Who in the world designed these meka here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why are we having the preliminary review here, by the way?

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: Why not conduct a review at the Fontaine Research Institute, you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: Well, it's because of that huge explosion, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: After the Institute blew up, the roads that led here from the Court of Fontaine were cut off for the most part. Not to mention the area around the Institute itself... They're a total mess.

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: This is where Mr. Raimondo's project team was originally located, a place far enough from the center of the explosion to not be greatly impacted by it. You know, meaning "lots of people who are still alive."

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: You know what I mean. Even though most of the Fontaine Research Institute was destroyed... our offices must continue operating. Otherwise, who will rebuild it?

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: That's why they had him go back urgently, and also made the decision to seek assistance from adventurers.

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: We are also following the Institute's orders, and are here to receive adventurers that come here to apply.

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: Although many areas around the Institute have been cleaned up and it's about time we return to our offices...

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: Mr. Choiseul has stated otherwise: "There are many things to do and we should focus on a bigger picture. Stay where you are if possible."

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: ...And just like that, our tiny office wound up staying right here.

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: *sigh* I seriously wonder when I'll be able to return to the Institute...

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: This is it here. Hang on a second while I go find Ms. Conjat...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... What's that place... A building floating in the air?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon gets it! This must be one of those magical "I only want the second floor, just cut the first floor out!" buildings that you hear about in stories.

choices.text: The Fontaine Research Institute's science is the finest in the world!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It really is!

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: *sigh* What you're seeing now is the Central Laboratory of the Fontaine Research Institute... Or should I say, what was once the Central Laboratory.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Mr. Edwin Eastinghouse was once within, trying to develop a field generator using Arkhium. Initial estimates indicated that the device could lift an entire block of buildings.

choices.text: My guess is that the experiment didn't turn out so well.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Of course, had Mr. Edwin not left two-thirds of the Fontaine Research Institute in ashes, he would've been a shoo-in for the post of the next Director.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: And today, the heavy responsibilities that belong to the post of Director, including a lifelong stipend and private dwelling, must be borne by the likes of Choiseul and Raimondo.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, Paimon wonders just what kind of people Raimondo and Choiseul are...

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: According to the evaluations of my peers, they are the type who can speak to you for an entire day without saying anything. I want to put that to the test.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: So, it is exceedingly accurate to say that Mr. Choiseul's talents are irreplaceable.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: #Look, {NICKNAME}. The location of your final review is the former location of the Alain Guillotin Research Institute, and now the current residence of the Institute.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Before the incident, weekly lectures were held there regarding critical projects. Of course, the old administrative functions are all still in effect, and can handle the final review.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's that plaza for? There are even seats around it... Is it an amphitheater of some kind?

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: Ah! I have heard colleagues stationed at the Institute speak of this place! That is the sacred ground to Fontainians, the place where Fonta was born!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Refreshing Fonta, a Font of Refreshment!"

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: *ahem* That is the Fontaine Research Institute's Academic Assembly Hall, and is dedicated to the purpose of displaying the fruits of our research. Such as the combat-capable Artificed Dancers, the gramophone, and Turbine-Powered Glider, among others.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: Previous analyses of Institute assets show that, of the items I mentioned previously, Fonta may be the only scientific achievement that remains legally profitable.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: I couldn't help but notice your wording contained a few baseless accusations.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: I'm glad you noticed. In that case, would you mind giving me your opinion of the ongoing criminal activity of selling off research materials from within the Institute?

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: It is absolutely vile, and those involved in the matter ought to be arrested in accordance with the law.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: Huh. Well, then, out of those with access to the Institute's technical assets and the capacity to commit such a crime, who do you believe it was exactly? Could it be possible that it was...

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: It was a criminal.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, let's keep moving.

response.speaker: Nacker

dialogues.speaker: Chronie

dialogues.speaker: Chalmet

response.speaker: Nacker

response.speaker: Chalmet

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, as I recall, you were an adventurer who came for the recruitment, yes? Well... when assisting our Institute in its work, you'll sometimes be required to carry out certain... precise operations.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: I'd like to see your practical capabilities first. Could you please go and help Ms. Chalmet operate the Energy Transfer Terminal to clear the area where the Survey Anchor is of obstructions?

choices.text: I guess I could...

response.speaker: Player

response.speaker: Nacker

response.speaker: Nacker

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Please follow her instructions and unblock the area as soon as you can. I'll be watching you from the side.

choices.text: So, the review has already begun?
Let's... deal with the Survey Anchor first, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Heinry
dialogues.text: Hey! Maybe my original documentation for the design of Fonta is in the ruins!

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Excellent work, the lock has been opened! Your abilities to quickly grasp the mechanics and execute are both outstanding, and your value far exceeds the vast majority of those who participate in experiments. I will truthfully report your performance as such.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what's next... Whoa! Ms. Chronie, what's gotten into you?

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Um... Ugh! I suddenly... feel like I'm gonna throw up... Ugh!

dialogues.speaker: Chalmet
dialogues.text: Ms. Chronie, please, drink this medicine. Exposed Survey Anchors radiate with Arkhium energy traces, and the place we are in now has also been affected somewhat.

dialogues.speaker: Chalmet
dialogues.text: However, this energy level won't leave permanent adverse effects on the body. Just take this medicine and you'll be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Blech! It tastes terrible. Forget it. I guess this is also a kind of first-hand experience...

dialogues.speaker: Chalmet
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, these two bottles are for the two of you. Please drink them quickly.

choices.text: I'm feeling fine. Let Paimon drink it.

response.speaker: Paimon

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Really? That's really quite interesting, and is completely at odds with the results of the "Applications of Arkhium Risk Report: 3rd Edition." We all should have been affected by the same amount of Arkhium energy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Harrumph! We're constantly journeying over mountains and seas... We're way stronger than the people you've got working here!

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Correction: You can now assume that all of the Fontaine Research Institute's staff are now working out in the open, beneath the sun and stars. Your report might consider mentioning the difficult work conditions we are enduring, Ms. Chronie.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: Ah! I've been wronged without having been notified in advance! The Steambird won't just let this go!

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: #Putting this all aside, you clearly have an extremely strong innate tolerance of the energy flow, {NICKNAME}. If so, you are certainly the best candidate to assist the Institute, without question.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Please approach the storage room, and report any dizziness, nausea, itchiness, or any other discomfort you feel during the process.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: #Hold on there! Are you using {NICKNAME} as a guinea pig? Without fulfilling your obligation to inform {M#him}{F#her} of the risks first?

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: #It is clearly stated in "Institute (abbr.) Externally Contracted Employee Agreement, Appendix C.41," which {M#he}{F#she} signed!

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Prior to being officially employed, the applicant shall be subject to a harmless Arkhium energy flow tolerance test, and the Institute has the right to terminate the contract based upon the results of said test.

choices.text: I hate reading text.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: You chose not to exercise your right to read the text, but each document was clearly marked, "Please sign your name after carefully reading the document and making sure there are no mistakes."

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: However, seeing as you seem completely unaffected by the energy flow... I believe you may be just the person we're looking for.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: In any case, let's get down to business. Take three steps toward the storage room, then hold still for thirty seconds.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You follow Nacker's series of complicated instructions and slowly approach the storage room at a steady pace.\nHowever, just like before, you don't feel any discomfort.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've gone this far, but Paimon still doesn't feel anything. Do you feel any discomfort?

choices.text: Ah! My head! It feels like it's gonna explode!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Huh!? What's wrong? {NICKNAME}, are you alright!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Pfft...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, okay, that was good acting! You nearly fooled Paimon there, sheesh... But...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, that's a relief, then. Paimon was worrying about how she'd carry you out of here if you were to suddenly pass out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Although, we've come all this way, and we can't see Nacker or the others anymore, and it doesn't seem like we can hear them either. What do we do next?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knows! Maybe they'll chuck some sort of box in here and communicate with us through that!

choices.text: That would be quite handy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll find out soon enough! Heh, Paimon can't wait to see what kind of cool gadgets they might use to communicate with us...

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: #{NICKNAME}! Can you hear me!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! So they rely on the technology of shouting really loud!

choices.text: I can hear you!

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Do you guys feel any discomfort!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Everything's good!

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: That's great! Please continue on to the Survey Anchor. You should be able to see it now!

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Once you retrieve it, it will temporarily fall into a dormant state and stop radiating energy, and then we'll be able to come in! *cough*... Ahem...

response.speaker: Paimon

response.text: We can hear you!

choices.text: Do they even have technology that cool?

response.text: Paimon neither!

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: You... actually managed to retrieve the Survey Anchor without any instruments, like it was nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Chalmet
dialogues.text: That's amazing. The last time, we needed at least three of us acting together to retrieve an Anchor.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Haha! I'm most certain that you're exactly the talent we've been looking for. With your help, all of our work is going to go much more smoothly.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll keep it for now. Let's leave this place and report back to the institute post-haste.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hang on, where's Ms. Chronie? Paimon doesn't see her anywhere...

dialogues.speaker: Chalmet
dialogues.text: She was feeling nauseous, so she stayed up there to rest.

dialogues.speaker: Chalmet
dialogues.text: But don't worry, she's already taken her medicine. She just needs a little time...

dialogues.speaker: Chalmet
dialogues.text: Huh? Ms. Chronie, what are you doing here...

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: A bunch of meka monsters suddenly showed up outside! They're on my heels, about to storm in!

choices.text: Well, thank you for that!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Look out, {NICKNAME}! Over there!

choices.text: Leave it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Chalmet
dialogues.text: The Central Laboratory ruins exploded? ...Just what happened?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: #Phew... luckily {NICKNAME} was here. These were probably the clockwork meka that the Institute used before to monitor energy flow, as they're equipped with Arkhium energy flow monitoring devices.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Although they're now out of control, they still automatically converged here upon detecting the energy flow from Arkhium...

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Mr. Nacker, should the Fontaine Research Institute be held accountable for these out-of-control meka in the wilds?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: I don't object to that at all. They should be held accountable...

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Oh?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: If you truly have a way to have those buried in the ground rise up and speak again.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Also, I sincerely suggest that you stay here and rest, Ms. Chronie. Mr. Choiseul and Raimondo are at the Institute's new site, and they aren't going anywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Once you're feeling better, then you can go and interview them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! You felt so sick that you could barely even stand. Don't push yourself too hard.

dialogues.text: Your health is essential.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: No... I can't. Interviewing Choiseul is the final step, not the beginning.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: That's why I'm following Mr. Nacker around... I... I want to experience everything firsthand and get tangible evidence.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: I have to question Choiseul with evidence in hand. That way, he won't be able to beat around the bush like last time.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Hehe, and lo and behold, I've now personally experienced this so-called "harmless" Arkhium energy flow, no?

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Once I get to the Fontaine Research Institute, I'm definitely going to uncover all... all of the hidden truths...

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: ...*sigh* I truly admire your professionalism, Ms. Chronie, but are you sure you'll be able to make it the rest of the way there?

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'll be right behind you guys. I'm a reporter, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Chalmet
dialogues.text: Hello! Mr. Nacker has already told me that you're here to learn how to operate the Energy Transfer Terminal. Is that right?

dialogues.speaker: Chalmet
dialogues.text: I've written the operating instructions down for you. Feel free to take a look at them.

dialogues.speaker: Chalmet
dialogues.text: Um... good luck with your assessment.

dialogues.text: Alright, there seems to really not be anything of value here... It's time to move on.

dialogues.text: A researcher who once worked together with Edwin Eastinghouse is now kicking storage drums around in a junk heap...

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Meanwhile, the Fontaine Research Institute still complains about being short-handed, huh... The way these researchers go about things is truly unfathomable.

dialogues.text: Everybody's worth is reflected in different ways, and "kicking storage drums" is my way of doing so these days.

dialogues.text: Eh!? You were that powerful!?

dialogues.text: That no longer means anything. Now I'm merely someone who was fortunate to survive this project, and one of the culprits who turned the Central Laboratory into what it is today.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: If the Survey Anchors really are that dangerous, why would you place them in a room? You know, it feels like you're... placing a coffee maker.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: I've already repeatedly emphasized that as long as you follow operating procedures correctly, you should not be at any risk of direct contact with said energy flows!

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: As for why they're locked up in a room... Well, it's to prevent certain idiots from taking any Anchors away without authorization, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: They have no idea how they work and just figure that they might sell some shiny things for a profit.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: We've hung up signs, distributed flyers, and even specially organized a lecture to try to tell everyone that not only were they worthless, but they could also do you harm.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: Ah, Nacker! It's great to see you. Have you taken care of those Survey Anchors?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: I trust that you've done as you always have — complete your tasks to perfection.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: I have. Allow me to give you two a brief report...

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: #With {NICKNAME}'s assistance, the Anchor was successfully retrieved without any equipment.

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: That's unbelievable! You were able to retrieve one without the use of any instruments? Goodness! Thank heavens.

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: The entire Institute right now only has three complete sets of such equipment, and I was honestly worried as to how we might retrieve the Anchors as soon as possible.

response.text: What I'd really like to know is... Why the Fontaine Research Institute would place these Survey Anchors to monitor the Arkhium energy flow after the explosion?

response.text: Ms. Chronie talks so fast! Like...

response.text: Allow me to be more specific. How exactly is the Fontaine Research Institute planning to deal with this explosion?

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: Uh... yes, I was just about to answer that question. This was an excellent question to ask, as many people... are concerned about it...

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Ms. Chronie, I am so delighted that you've come to visit again. I must stress on behalf of Mr. Choiseul that the institute has never changed its solution to the explosion.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Once we have recovered all of the retrievable research assets at the old site, we will demolish the old Central Laboratory and do our best to restore the area's natural environment to its original state.

response.text: By the Central Laboratory, you mean that building floating in the air? How are you going to demolish a building like that?

choices.text: Shoot it down with a cannon?

response.text: Of course we shan't be using such crude and simple solutions. This demolition will utilize our newly-researched "Experimental Field Generator."

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: This device can deactivate the Gravity-Altering Field that surrounds the Institute's ruins and land them on the ground safely...

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: But wasn't this device also within said ruins? And wasn't it also a work of Edwin Eastinghouse that used... Arkhium as its energy source...?

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: So, based on what you're saying, the Fontaine Research Institute is still unwilling to give up this "harmless" Arkhium project, yes?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think they're not giving it up so easily.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y—You've been keeping up with what she's saying?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Nope, I just repeated her last sentence.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Have you been doing this to pretend that you understand what's going on?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, anyways, the Fontaine Research Institute is still trying to do dangerous stuff in dangerous ways, right?

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: A great summary, Ms. Paimon.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: If we're discussing uncontrolled risks, well, even walking on a road may be dangerous. Also, you should note that the energy source we're using is the completely new and stable Tri-State Arkhium.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: How does that differ from normal Arkhium? Does the new word in front of it mean anything? This, to me, seems like a purely rhetorical maneuver.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: I'm sure Mr. Choiseul would be happy to have an in-depth conversation with you about grammar, but I've left Mr. Nacker hanging for too long. And really that's just impolite.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Mr. Nacker, I trust that you've done everything that I've asked?

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: #With {NICKNAME}'s help, everything couldn't have gone any better.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: ...Hmm, is this an adventurer who came for recruitment?

response.text: #...That is rare. Extremely rare. I'm delighted that you're applying for work at the Institute, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: After hundreds of years of bad luck, we're finally catching a break... I'm confident that you'll be of great help to us.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Here are the documents I signed...

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Ah, leave them over there. Don't worry about them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Aren't you going to take a look at them? We spent ages on them, and Mr. Desnos also took them very seriously...

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Hahaha, these documents definitely have their uses. They certainly help us weed idiots out, at least.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: As for you, however... I believe that your good qualities go far beyond what they can summarize. So let's leave them alone for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, are you saying we passed the review?

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Without a doubt, yes.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: I will personally prepare the contract and notice that you'll need to sign for follow-up work. Until then... Mr. Nacker?

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Yes?

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: While Ms. Chronie appears to be having a discussion about energy safety with Mr. Choiseul...

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: #How about you take {NICKNAME} to retrieve the last two Survey Anchors?

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: The energy flow control operations are nearing completion, all that's left is to compile the data. *sigh* Oh well, at least it's under control...

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: ...Are you guys heading somewhere else? I'll come along too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This reporter lady sure has pretty good ears...

choices.text: Blow it up, just like before?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Looks like we've really got the right person for the job this time. Put them over here. Someone will come and handle them.
