dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Th—They're so thick! Why are there so many documents!?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Because no matter how one looks at it, escorting a researcher into the ruins of the Fontaine Research Institute and then landing said ruins shall be no small matter.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: And since it is such an important matter, it is only natural for us to explain every detail to the one carrying out the work.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who am I escorting?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Why that'd be Mr. Nacker, of course. Across the entire Institute, there's no one better suited than him to deal with the Central Laboratory ruins.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: I request that I accompany Mr. Nacker.

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: What? Uh, I think...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: ...This is a terrific proposal.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Choiseul, did you forget what we mentioned when we came up with the plan? We must keep the public informed about the rebuilding of the Institute with the utmost transparency.

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: Uh... that's right! The new Fontaine Research Institute has nothing to hide. Edwin made some mistakes, but we're past that now.

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: Please go report on it. Go to the ruins of the Institute and see the mistakes Edwin Eastinghouse made.

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: Looking back again, the Institute now is just what we've been working toward, the cause we stand for! But allow me to emphasize once again that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And here we go again... Paimon's about to fall asleep...

choices.text: I truly admire how much you guys have to say.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not to mention how every sentence seems to magically make people fall asleep... Paimon's already feeling sleepy from just half a sentence...

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: No, no, it's important business. So please, come this way...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Under Raimondo's guidance, you sign many complicated documents. Thanks to your prior experience, you finish signing them before you know it this time...

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: #...Alright, that should be all of them. Thank you, {NICKNAME}. You are now an Externally Contracted Assistant Researcher for the Fontaine Research Institute.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What about Paimon? Does Paimon get any title?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're my important assistant, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Assistant... Ugh, that just doesn't sound cool...

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Hahaha! Don't worry. Assistants play an absolutely critical role within the Institute.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: But let us get back to business, shall we? Things right now in the Institute are... rather complicated. The matters you'll be dealing with are also urgent, so I won't keep you for much longer.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: While you're on the way, Mr. Nacker will inform you of some things to note, as well as what you will actually need to do.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: The rest is up to you now. A lot rests on your shoulders, Mr. Nacker.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: #...Well then, please follow me, {NICKNAME}. We must get to the ruins.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure thing!

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: Don't forget me!

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Yes, and you. How could I possibly forget you?

choices.text: Maybe you should call me after you're done talking...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, this doesn't have anything to do with us — and this is a good time for a break, anyway.

talks.objective: Go to the ruins of the Fontaine Research Institute

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: #Come on, {NICKNAME}, Ms. Chronie, this way.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: ...So, you mean we're going to delve into this... this... uh, this patch of water?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: That's right. With the help of this "allogravity-condensed water," we can ascend the ruins of the Institute safely and efficiently.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: If you don't wish to do it that way, you may also go to the opposite bank and glide in from the highest mountain using a wind glider.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Forget it. I... I'm not that good at using a wind glider, and I'm not really... used to heights, either.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Very well. Now I'll go over a few things to keep in mind when it comes to allogravity-condensed water.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Nacker details considerations when making use of said allogravity-condensed water.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So in a nutshell, it's the same as when swimming or diving.

choices.text: I feel like this is more "flying or diving."

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: I suppose you could call it "anti-gravity diving" if you had to.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Is everybody ready? Ms. Chronie, you can still back out now if you'd like, and simply wait here for us to return.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: Reporters never back down. I'll be right behind you guys! I'll... try to, anyway...

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Alright then, if you insist. Let's get going now.

choices.text: Diving in midair will be quite a novelty.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: In that case, please do enjoy experiencing it for yourself.

talks.objective: Go to the ruins of Fontaine Research Institute

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This... What's this large plate?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: That's the Experimental Field Generator that Mr. Edwin developed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Didn't it already blow up? It looks perfectly fine now.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: The thing that exploded wasn't this machine but the Arkhium ore that powers its core driver, the Arkhium Kinetic Core.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This thing... Will it suddenly start moving by itself?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Relax. This big guy can't move now that it's lost its power supply.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But didn't Raimondo say that we needed to use it to make the ruins descend? If it can't move...

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Only a part of it will be activated. The Tri-State Arkhium can only support its operation at half speed, but that should be enough to relieve the abnormal gravity state the Central Laboratory ruins are in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Er... Paimon doesn't understand that at all...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you need us to do?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Please follow me. The place where we will need to work is in the back.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Ms. Chronie, please stay here. Some areas in the back contain Insitute secrets, and you're not allowed to have any exposure to them.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: I can see that "back" of yours from here. What secrets could be hidden inside?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: I have no idea either. That's why you're definitely not allowed inside.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: What nonsense!

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Anyway, please wait here. If you take photos randomly, you might capture something related to Institute secrets.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: For example... the, um... formula for the sugar-free berry-flavored Fonta. This new Fonta product is quite important to the Institute.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: If you leak any information of it to the outside world, you'll need to undergo a one-month confidential investigation and must report to the Maison Gestion at the Palais Mermonia three times every day and be questioned...

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Of course, you'll need to stop your journalistic work.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Hahaha, don't worry. Even if I get taken away by the Palais Mermonia for questioning, it will only be because I've uncovered the secret you're hiding.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: I won't let myself be forced to stop working for a reason as absurd as leaking some Fonta formula.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: I admire your work ethic. I hope everything goes well with your photo-taking.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, let's go. There's still work for us to do.

talks.objective: Defeat all of the malfunctioning meka

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Sometimes I really don't get why the Institute had to design the support clockwork meka to look like humans.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Just from the perspective of supporting research, hands and feet are far worse than tracking and multifunctional clockwork meka apertures.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's this rock?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Oh, this is the Arkhium that supplies energy to the Experimental Field Generator.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: What restrains it is the energy supply device created by Mr. Edwin. See this here? This circuit connects to the Generator.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Of all the inert Arkhium we found, this one was the best in terms of purity and stability.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And then boom it went.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: That came down to Mr. Edwin. I trust that this wasn't the cause, or at least, it shouldn't take all the blame.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... I—It's not gonna blow up again, is it?

choices.text: When that happens, I'm gonna need you to take us to the skies, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't have super strength! But... if it really does blow up, then P—Paimon could give it a shot...

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Hahaha, don't worry. Now that Mr. Edwin's not around, we're completely safe.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Alright, I'm about to use Raimondo's catalyst to transform this Arkhium into Tri-State Arkhium and activate that big fellow outside.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Then, these ruins should be able to safely land on the ground.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, could you please help me take some photos in the area? I need to use them as evidence for my work record.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Didn't you just say taking photos wasn't allowed?

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: It's fine. These will be used for reference in the Institute and won't be distributed.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Unless you secretly keep a few for yourself... which I trust you won't do.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Oh, right, and when you're taking photos, please look for Ms. Chronie while doing so. I've got no idea where she's run off to... or where she's hiding.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: I really don't want to start the Generator only to suddenly find a lady tossed into midair.

choices.text: When that happens, let's jump into the water below.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Jumping into water from a high place such as this is gonna hurt when we, y'know, "splash"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Worst case scenario, P—Paimon will tug on your clothes and help to absorb the impact...?

talks.objective: Use a Kamera to take pictures and document the area

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Readings are normal... Looks like everything's fine, and we shouldn't come across any hiccups...

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, once you're done taking photos, please go find Ms. Chronie.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: I'll come to find you guys when I've finished making adjustments here.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: How suspicious...

choices.text: What's suspicious? Show me too!

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: #Oh! {NICKNAME}, you gave me a fright. How are you able to walk around without making any noise?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You were just too focused! Speaking of it, you followed us all the way here. Have you managed to find anything?

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: Not really. Since Mr. Nacker said all that, I don't really want to get in trouble.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: In the end, all I could take pictures of were these dilapidated houses, broken rocks, and a motionless machine...

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: I bet I would be able to take photos of a big scoop if I could fly in the air just like you can, Paimon.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why be a reporter if you can fly?

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: I was born to do this. It's the reason I exist.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: I, too, am very sure of that, Ms. Chronie.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: What? You're also able to walk without making any noise? Is this a new technology the Institute's developed?

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: #Unfortunately, we don't teach walking courses. I've already completed all the preparations, in any case. {NICKNAME}, please take Ms. Chronie back to the Institute.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Once the Experimental Field Generator is activated, it will rapidly change the gravity in the surrounding area.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: I've been through professional training, and I know what to do in this situation.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: For your safety, it would be best if you stay away from here.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And how are you going to get down?

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: You don't need to worry about me. Mr. Edwin taught me how to use the Generator personally.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: No one in the Institute can control this big guy as freely as I can... Not even Raimondo.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Guess we'll have to leave it to a professional then. Be careful!

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Go now. We'll meet again on the surface.

choices.text: Hi, Ms. Chronie!

dialogues.speaker: Desnos
dialogues.text: What happened? How did it explode again...

talks.objective: Go back to the Fontaine Research Institute and report to Raimondo

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! You're back. How's the work coming along?

choices.text: Everything's going swimmingly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There are still some finishing touches that "ought to be left to a professional," so Mr. Nacker is still up there.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I feel like I haven't really contributed that much...

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: #Don't say that. You're our safety rope! Without you, dear {NICKNAME}, how could we have dared let Mr. Nacker go up there by himself? It could be said that the trip was a brilliant success.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: There were other benefits as well. Ms. Chronie's managed to photograph some... thought-provoking images, that she would like to ask me about. And a few of those pictures should prove even more "interesting" for Mr. Nacker.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Let's not talk about that for now. Come, let us take a photo together. Monsieur Choiseul will also need to present you with a certificate and an honorary title.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Honorary title?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, ooh, and what about Paimon? Paimon... will also get a promotion from assistant, right!?

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: #Uh, seeing as... you're {NICKNAME}'s companion, then I guess you could join in on the photo. As for the title...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So there's no honorary title for Paimon, then?

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Honorary titles must remain limited in quantity and stay relatively rare. Otherwise, how would we get sponsors and support through awarding them?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... Alright then...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then allow me to award Paimon...

choices.text: The honorary title of "Best Companion."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, just what kind of nonsense titles are those! ...Hmph, we're already best buddies, Paimon doesn't need a title for that!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You better make {NICKNAME}'s really awesome!

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Of course. This honorary title is of the highest standing. Besides, haven't you also been promoted to Assistant to the Honorary Senior Researcher? Come on, let's get that photo taken.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: An assistant's still an assistant, no matter how many words you put after it...

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Alright, let's take the photo. This is an occasion to remember.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Monsieur Choiseul, you're...

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Ooh, looks like he's having a nice conversation with Ms. Chronie.

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: ...Hence, this operation is a stepping stone to rebuilding the Institute. We can do it, and it is our duty to do so, as it has always been!

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: As for the former site of the Institute, we will keep it preserved forever and rebuild it as the Fontaine Research Institute Safety Education Center.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: ...I think I've just about had enough.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: #I'm certain that everybody has benefited from your speech, Monsieur Choiseul. But now's the time to take a photo together with {NICKNAME}, wouldn't you say?

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: Yes, of course! We must take a photo and mark this occasion with our dear Honorary Senior Researcher of the Fontaine Research Institute!

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: Please give us a second, Ms. Chronie. This shouldn't take too long.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: Oh, don't worry. It's not like the things you said just now weren't all cliches anyway.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: Weren't you guys going to take a photo together? I just so happen to have a Kamera with me. Please go and stand in position.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: I traveled a long way to get here, so please at least make it worth the trip, okay?

choices.text: The honorary title of "Best Travel Guide."
A super awesome title!
It's fine.

dialogues.speaker: Chalmet
dialogues.text: The backup medicine is also nearly finished. I'll go back and get more from the Institute later...

dialogues.speaker: Chalmet
dialogues.text: Wait, do we even have any medicine left...?

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Uh... was that an... explosion just now?

choices.text: What else could it have been...

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: I... don't believe that was an explosion. All things considered, uh... it was probably a controllable...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That was an explosion! Paimon was nearly blown away just now. If not, what else could it have been!?

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: Mr. Choiseul! Could you please explain this to us. Was this something that you had anticipated?

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: I... uh... I must say, you asked a... very good question, a very... excellent one... as... many people are wondering the same thing.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: ...The color of these bodies of water. Could it be that the condenser components are already in...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait, Nacker hasn't come down yet!

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: ...You're right, he hasn't returned yet.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: #Let's not delay, {NICKNAME}. We need to go now.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: Wait! I want to go too! The truth behind this explosion...

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Please do not act rashly, Miss Reporter. If you dip one of your toes into that water, you'll be saying goodbye to this world within a minute.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: Don't scare me!

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Would you! Please! Just! Stay! Here!

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, according to your previous experience, the energy flow that remains in these bodies of water shouldn't affect you too much.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Please get to the ruins as quickly as you can. I'll find my own way up, and I'll meet you there.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Your own way?

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: I have my ways. After the explosion, I was among one of the first up there to conduct disaster investigation and evaluation.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Things at that time were much more complicated than they are now... Anyway, enough talk. Let's get moving. Hopefully, Mr. Nacker won't meet the same fate that Edwin did...

choices.text: We're just taking a photo together. Is such a ceremonious greeting necessary?

dialogues.speaker: Vuillermoz
dialogues.text: It's over, it's all over now...

talks.objective: Go to the ruins of the Fontaine Research Institute
Defeat all of the malfunctioning meka

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: It looks like the Arkhium overloaded, and that the cooling mechanism is also damaged. Nacker... What have you done here exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: This was my fault. I didn't think that Nacker would still be unsatisfied, despite all the benefits I gave him...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Benefits? Wait a second...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Why are you looking at me like that? Did he say anything to you?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Raimondo of your encounters with Nacker, and his attitudes toward various matters...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Hmph... Sweet talk! Did he tell you guys, then, that it was people like him — Edwin's successors — who are reaping the benefits of this mess by stealing all kinds of information and selling it for a fortune?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... You guys are telling completely different stories. Paimon doesn't know who to believe anymore. If only he were here, then we could find out the truth. Paimon doesn't see him at all, though...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If he's not here, where could he have gone?

choices.text: Maybe he successfully escaped.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: I don't think he was killed at the very least... I'll explain why later. For now, though, we must stabilize this Arkhium as quickly as we can.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: The suppression system shut down, and the ore is presently in an excited state. That is what caused the explosion.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What caused the explosion? But this big rock doesn't look blown up at all.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I don't understand...

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Alright... I agree that this is indeed quite difficult to understand. I'll explain it in simpler terms for you... I guess I have no choice now.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: The Experimental Field Generator that Edwin created is extremely powerful and can manipulate gravity... This I believe you know already.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: After the explosion, all the Arkhium in the institute shattered into fragments. Among these fragments, many of them could have turned into an excited state and triggered an explosion at any time.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: With the use of Gravity Fields... they were all restrained and gathered... beneath our feet.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: That explosion just before was a small one caused by a small part of Arkhium in the ruins that was affected by energy flow. I guess you could call it... a minor rehearsal of a third great explosion.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... huh? Then... this ruin is a...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Super-huge, ready-to-explode piece of Arkhium!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: S—So you guys did all this... not because you wanted to retrieve assets, but because you were scared this place would explode again!?

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: ...That's just one of the objectives of this operation. But right now, our priority is to retrieve the condensing components that fell into the water and restart the suppression device.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: There is also Arkhium inside those components, and the intense energy flow has likely caused... unpredictable changes to the water bodies.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Forgive me, but I'm really not capable of retrieving them and installing them back on the inhibitor.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: #Only you are capable of doing this, {NICKNAME}. Please, for the Court of Fontaine, and...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Since it's urgent, I'll just get the job done first...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But once this is all over, you'd better explain everything clearly!

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: If all goes well, I will tell you everything I know.

choices.text: Maybe he's already...

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Huh? What was Nacker doing...?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: ...That Mr. Nacker really knows how to create trouble for others. Just like that boss of his, Edwin Eastinghouse!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: We really can't catch a break here. Not only did the explosion break off the condensing components of the device, but it also destroyed the self-sustaining system of the inhibitor.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: I'm about to remove the two backup Pneumousia Cores in the Experimental Field Generator and use them to supply energy to the inhibitor.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Luckily this big fella can't move. Otherwise, we wouldn't even have time to run...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's just not moving right now, you mean.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, knock on wood! Don't say things like that! What if it actually starts moving?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Don't worry, its main source of energy is that big chunk of Arkhium behind it.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Although the Arkhium has transformed into an activated state, the explosion damaged all of the energy supply lines, so it's lost all of its energy supply...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: ...Huh? The Arkhium Kinetic Core should've been right here. Where did...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Hold on, you said that the Pneumousia Cores were a backup energy source.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A—And isn't the activation condition for backup energy sources... the complete loss of energy?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Oh. Uh oh...

talks.objective: Shut off the Experimental Field Generator

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It... it stopped...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: I knew you could do it! Quick, grab these two cores. Let's go hook up the power.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Just like before, you go connect the energy source, and I'll adjust the device.

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: Raimondo, during our last meeting, did I really mention that we must keep the public informed about the rebuilding of the institute with the utmost transparency?

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: I really don't remember that. Perhaps I should check for it in the meeting notes. Could you tell me what page it was exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: If by "checking for it in the meeting notes," you mean you wish to see this point made in clear writing...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Then I must say that it won't happen, as such a point cannot be summarized into a single sentence.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: This point was made based on the overall essence of that meeting, which was to first address morality and human relations, and the sum total of social norms...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Lastly, this concept, when extracted from countless specific words and actions, is so broad and generic that anyone can see and comprehend its abstract concept.

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: So what you're saying is, "I didn't say that?"

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Correct.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Finally, it's stabilized. The Arkhium has transformed into an inert state... We and the Fontaine Research Institute are safe, for now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But it seems there are ever more secrets.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: As for the things you'd like to know, I will be happy to answer. But... not right now.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: What I can tell you now, based on my hypothesis, is that... Mr. Nacker stole the Arkhium Kinetic Core and triggered this small explosion.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: But before explaining in too much detail, we should return to the Institute, and place the proper notation and partitions into this interlude.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: ...Or at the very least, we need to stop Miss Journalist from getting more deeply involved. The Arkhium Kinetic Core is connected to too many other matters, and we must handle it in complete confidentiality.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: So, I would like you to "cooperate" with my work.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Cooperate with your work?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You... you're not saying to play along with your lies, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The scarier something is, the more you should share it with others! Then, we can all work together to deal with it faster!

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: I have my doubts about that, you two. Every matter has its own way of being dealt with, and in this instance, we must first call for silence.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: But I promise that I would never have you steer from your moral standards or demand that you... have the same standard of behavior as we do.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: All I ask is for you to remain quiet. You need not do anything else. You might be wondering why I would have you remain silent while telling you the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: I'll just come out and say it now. Your coming here is the only good fortune that our Institute has had in nearly a hundred years.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: No matter what happens or what the cost is, we must maintain good relations with you. I'm sure Mr. Choiseul feels the same way.

choices.text: Is telling the truth also a "cost" as far as you're concerned?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! You're only just telling us the truth now, which you should have done ages ago. Just what sorta "cost" is that?

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: #Dear {M#sir}{F#lady}, Paimon. Telling the truth honestly is, in truth, the greatest price one can pay.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Let's go back. I ask sincerely for your understanding and to provide all... necessary cooperation.

choices.text: Is transparency something you'd consider a "cost" as well?

talks.objective: Return to the Fontaine Research Institute

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Let's cooperate with Raimondo for now...)

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: #No need to bother {NICKNAME} anymore, Ms. Chronie. Allow me to explain the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Don't even think of trying to get away with it, Mr. Raimondo. I saw the Arkhium with my own eyes. This explosion must have been caused by it.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Did you not repeatedly emphasize before, that all the Arkhium had been properly processed and disposed of? Just what are you hiding?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: I haven't hidden anything. This explosion was always a "controllable hazard removal directional blast."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C—Controllable hazard... wait, hazard removal... What?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mind you all don't bite your tongues on that.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: It basically means to use small, controlled blasts to quickly remove Arkhium fragments.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: With the goal of activating the Experimental Field Generator as quickly as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: But I couldn't have imagined... that Mr. Nacker would steal the Arkhium Kinetic Core needed to start the Experimental Field Generator.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Not only that, but he intentionally activated that large chunk of Arkhium, using it to draw our attention while he made his escape.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: ...So, is that the ploy you came up with just now? To dump all the blame onto a researcher, who could be dead right now for all you know!?

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: I think what you really want to hide is that you are completely incapable of dealing with the Arkhium! The Arkhium is still a major threat to the Court of Fontaine!

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Ridiculous! A person's life isn't something you can throw away to help spread your own lies!

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: I have already told you the truth, Ms. Chronie... Please listen to a final word of advice.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: It takes only the slightest bit of effort to fixate on something, but it always takes more brain power to avert your gaze from it.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: ...Enough. I won't listen to another word you say, nor will I dwell on this.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Your words, deeds, and all the facts concealed by the Institute will be reported on in the next issue of The Steambird. Good day, gentlemen.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Ms. Chronie strides away from the Fontaine Research Institute...

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: #...Thank goodness, that's finally over with... Oh, and thank you too, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I just did what I should.

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: Ah, such humility. In this day and age, those who do what they should are already outstanding.

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: You didn't make assumptions about whether something is good or bad based on your subjective thoughts. Instead, you... think carefully about what you do and say for the sake of the greater good! Truly an excellent person!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... is this really okay? Paimon still thinks that we should tell everyone the truth...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: #There's no need to bear such a heavy burden, dear {NICKNAME}. You only... cooperated, after listening to my repeated entreaties.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: I am a Senior Technician of the Fontaine Research Institute, and the responsibility for this matter falls squarely on me, and me alone.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But Ms. Chronie said...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: She has already obtained the truth she wants for herself. I wish her well.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: But as for us... we still have much to be concerned about. For example, the whereabouts of Mr. Nacker, and the Arkhium Kinetic Core...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Hahaha, but shouldn't we first give you a few awards as well, Monsieur Choiseul?

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: Right, right! Let's take another group photo together. The one we took before had an... unseemly explosion in the background.

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: This new photo must be decent enough to be worthy of your status as our Honorary Senior Researcher.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Choiseul and Raimondo stand in the same position as before, and an Institute researcher takes a photo for everyone...

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: Perfect! Look at us — a decent bunch of decent people!

choices.text: The ostentatious awards ceremony has finally ended...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon hopes we won't ever have to attend such a... pompous ceremony ever again...

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: This certificate and trophy are for you. I'll post a copy on the Institute bulletin board later.

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: *sigh* I hope our researchers will follow your example. On this path, we must strive to take the lead, overcome all obstacles, and put in 120% of our...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I actually have more questions for you.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Of course. I know what you want to ask. Even though your questions are all... um, extremely complicated, I'm willing to answer them.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: In any case, I believe we'll have more opportunities to work together in the future, Honorary Senior Researcher.

choices.text: The scene just isn't explosive enough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Stoppit! No more exploding! Any more explosions and Paimon'll have nightmares!

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: What should we do, Raimondo? Do you think we can convince this journalist? Tri-State Arkhium... I always felt that that name would bring us trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Choiseul, do you think that the name is not up to current grammatical standards and that people will criticize us for being superficial?

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: No! Tri-State Arkhium may be different from Arkhium in name, but it looks exactly the same no matter how one looks at it!

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: This is not a problem, as its internal structure is indeed different. The difference between it and Arkhium is like good guys and bad guys. They're both people, but they're very different in society.

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: Ah, Raimondo... People never bother to tell the good guys from the bad guys, much less the nature of a piece of rock.

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: They'll just say, hey, this rock looks like Arkhium, and it works like Arkhium, so why isn't it called Arkhium?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Relax, Choiseul. I've already prepared the explanation script.

choices.text: (Keep listening...)

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: See? "...The energy source that drives the Experimental Field Generator is not Arkhium, but a new one called Tri-State Arkhium."

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: "This type of ore is an inert variant of Arkhium that was created through a special transformation process. After entering the all-new 'silent excitement state,' it is much more stable than the original's excited state."

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: This won't do! They'll still just say that we're doing some kind of rhetorical trick!

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: "This rhetoric is also based on strict academic classification. All in all, you will witness its excellence after this display."

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: *sigh* But this certainly won't be able to satisfy that group of reporters.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: They can never be satisfied. Mr. Choiseul, all we need to do is put on a display... That's all.

choices.text: (Stop listening...)

dialogues.speaker: Denichere
dialogues.text: It's getting bad... again...

dialogues.speaker: Conjat
dialogues.text: This document needs to be filed, and this one rewritten... Ugh... There's just so much to do...

dialogues.speaker: Sevigne
dialogues.text: ...The Central Laboratory exploded again unexpectedly. Was Monsieur Edwin... actually researching bombs?

dialogues.speaker: Chalmet
dialogues.text: Huh? Back up here already? Have you retrieved the survey anchor?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: The Survey Anchor... hasn't been retrieved yet, I see. Have you come back up for a quick break?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: That's fine, but please retrieve it as soon as you can. We'd prefer to avoid further trouble, you see.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: ...This should be fine now.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Huh? Please take Ms. Chronie with you and go down quickly. I'll be activating this big guy in a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Then, this troublesome matter will be resolved once and for all.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Please follow her instructions and unblock the area as soon as you can. I'll be watching you from the side.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, how did it feel for you to be that close to a Survey Anchor?

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: If you feel any discomfort, then let me know immediately! I'll help you get the truth out there, even if Mr. Nacker tries to hide it.

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: Ms. Chronie, everything we do is in the best interests of the people of the Court of Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: ...So what you're saying is that the Fontaine Research Institute predicted the explosion just now? Are you kidding? Do you think I'm a Gestionnaire? You can't hoodwink me that easily!

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: I think Monsieur Choiseul has expressed himself clearly enough. The situation is still under control. The status quo of the Court of Fontaine will not be adversely affected.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Now, allow me to make a statement explaining the events that really occurred.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: That's enough, Mister! I don't believe you for a second!

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, you should have seen everything, right? I'm begging you, tell me the truth!

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: My goodness, was this also predicted? Oh my...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Let's think about this again first...)

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: ...How can I get up there? Also, will that medicine work?

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: But he said that as long as I touch it... And those pictures. Darn it... I need to think of a way...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Drat... The energy flow is too strong here. I need to take more medicine...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the real reason for the explosion at the Fontaine Research Institute...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: ...You are quite inquisitive, but now's not the time for a long conversation. Please go and retrieve the condensing components first.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll tell you the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: #...I'm all ears, my dear {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Chronie everything that has happened, from beginning to end, without omitting anything.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: About the large Arkhium and the Experimental Field Generator.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: About Nacker, who is missing and could be alive or dead, and about Raimondo's accusations of him having stolen the Arkhium Kinetic Core.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: And of course, what Raimondo cares most about, the Central Laboratory ruins that could explode again at any time.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: ...I'm shocked. Mr. Choiseul, were you aware of this?

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: I... Oh... Of course, I... Um, my goodness...

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: So the Fontaine Research Institute doesn't even have the courage to face their own mistakes? Just to cover up the fact that you couldn't deal with the Arkhium problem, you did absolutely everything you could...

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: #What I find most surprising is that you even tried to trick {NICKNAME}, who has been doing their utmost to help.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: #You even wanted to use {NICKNAME}'s credibility to convince me that Nacker was behind all of these crimes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? Chronie, did you really understand?

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: I completely understand everything, dear Paimon. Thank you for dropping such subtle hints for me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: H—Hints? Did... did we drop any hints?

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Of course, I know that what the Institute really wants to hide — the fact that the Central Laboratory ruins can explode again at any time.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Or to put it another way, Arkhium is still a threat to the entire Court of Fontaine!

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Ridiculous! A person's life isn't something you can throw away to help spread your own lies!

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: I have already told you the truth, Ms. Chronie... Please listen to a final word of advice.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: It takes only the slightest bit of effort to fixate on something, but it always takes more brain power to avert your gaze from it.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: ...Enough. I won't listen to another word you say, nor will I dwell on this.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Your words, deeds, and all the facts concealed by the Institute will be reported on in the next issue of The Steambird. Good day, gentlemen.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Ms. Chronie strides away from the Fontaine Research Institute...

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: #...Thank goodness, that's finally over with... Oh, and thank you too, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I didn't do what you asked me to. I thought you would...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: You thought I would throw a tantrum at you and scold you for not doing what I said?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: #My dear {NICKNAME}, since the very beginning, your job has only been to escort the researcher to the ruins for an expedition. What I asked you to do was above and beyond the call of duty.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: It would have been great if you kept your silence, as that would've saved us a lot of trouble in the future, yes.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: But it's not necessarily bad that you told her the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: I believe that now that Ms. Chronie has gotten what she wants, she will not bother us again for the time being.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She will tell the public everything.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: I believe she will do that. I hope the people of Fontaine will like the truth she publicizes.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: But as for us... we still have much to be concerned about. For example, the whereabouts of Mr. Nacker, and the Arkhium Kinetic Core...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Hahaha, but shouldn't we first give you a few awards as well. Monsieur Choiseul, would you do the honors?

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: Oh? Of course! That's right. I've already prepared everything. There's a certificate, trophy... and other forms of remuneration, too.

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: But before that, let's take a group photo together. The one we took before had an... unseemly explosion in the background.

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: This new photo must be decent enough to be worthy of your status as our Honorary Senior Researcher.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Choiseul and Raimondo stand in the same position as before, and an Institute researcher takes a photo for everyone...

dialogues.speaker: Choiseul
dialogues.text: Perfect! Look at us — a decent bunch of decent people!

choices.text: The ostentatious awards ceremony has finally ended...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon hopes we won't ever have to attend such a... pompous ceremony ever again...

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: This certificate and trophy are for you. I'll post a copy of the cert on the Institute bulletin board later.

response.speaker: Choiseul
response.text: *sigh* I hope our researchers will follow your example. On this path, we must strive to take the lead, overcome all obstacles, and put in 120% of our...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I actually have more questions for you.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: Of course. I know what you want to ask. Even though your questions are all... um, extremely complicated, I'm willing to answer them.

response.speaker: Raimondo
response.text: In any case, I believe we'll have more opportunities to work together in the future, Honorary Senior Researcher.

choices.text: The scene just isn't explosive enough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Stoppit! No more exploding! Any more explosions and Paimon'll have nightmares!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The kinetic core that disappeared must have been taken away by someone... If there's anyone who had the opportunity to commit this crime, it would probably be...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: After the explosion... Well, the previous one, researchers of Edwin's stripe don't seem to have been very well-received...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The explosion that happened when we were taking the photo was quite a shock... What could have caused it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Will it really be okay to let someone unsuitable for the role be the leader...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...The Arkhium has been activated from its inert state and is releasing a great amount of energy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's clear that Mr. Nacker is responsible for everything. He stole the kinetic core... which affected the activation of the Arkhium fragments.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There are many unrecovered activated fragments around the ruins of the Central Laboratory. The entire place is a huge, dangerous bomb!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It seems apparent that Nacker's the scapegoat of the current management system. He's a senior researcher, and yet he's been reduced to doing random tasks...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's obvious! The second explosion must have been caused by Mr. Choiseul and Mr. Raimondo's chaotic operations!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That shouldn't be the case...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This should be the place Katheryne marked for us, but there seems to be nothing here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, there seems to be someone...
Help! You over there! Don't just watch! Save me!

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: We're here. This is the Mary-Ann Memorial Park. Let's see if there are any assets that can be recovered in this area.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is a park, but it doesn't look like a park at all.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: When the explosion happened, this place was hit by the first shock waves, and most of the buildings here were destroyed.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: But there might've been some paper assets that survived the blast... That's what I'm hoping, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Let me see... Oh, there might be something under the storage drums over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this pile of storage drums... also Institute property?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: I guess so, but we'll need to remove them to see if there are more valuable assets here.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: What's up with these meka monsters? Why do they move sometimes and stop moving at others!?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: I fear that anyone who could've answered your question is now... well, indisposed.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: #Let's hurry over to the Institute. {NICKNAME} needs to participate in the final qualification review, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: This is the last Survey Anchor. Let's return to the Institute.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: I'm curious. Did any of the adventurers who responded to the recruitment come and get this kind of Survey Anchor?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Of course, and there were quite a few. This Survey Anchor retrieval test is part of the qualification review.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: After the initial phase of the qualification review, they will try to make contact with the Survey Anchors under the supervision of Institute researchers.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: They...

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: They consumed a lot of our antiemetics.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? Why are there so many meka here? We dismantled so many of them last time, didn't we?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: It seems that the explosion just now caused that Arkhium to release another wave of energy, which awakened another batch of clockwork meka...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: #Please do dismantle them, {NICKNAME}, and quickly, please.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! This big guy's moving! Gah, Paimon knew it would from the start!

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Edwin, you scoundrel! What did you do to this thing!?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, only you can turn it off now...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: But not to worry. There are only two Pneumousia Cores powering it right now, so it's only functioning at one-third of its full power!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #That's easy for you to say. Paimon can barely fly like this! Be careful, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Just what kinda place is this, it's all run-down and shabby...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Wait, it seems like there's someone over there...
Help! You over there! Don't just watch! Save me!

dialogues.speaker: Chisseray
dialogues.text: Sure enough... Not doing research any more was the correct decision...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Punched Tape...

dialogues.speaker: Chisseray
dialogues.text: Punched Tape? Now? The Central Laboratory blew up again! Sorry, but before that's cleared up, I don't have any time to worry about that stuff...
